notes.made: Loggins and Michael McDonald had a melody they liked and, by Loggins's count, wrote the lyric four times as a love song and threw each one out. It came together after Loggins visited his father, who was facing another round of vascular surgery and seemed ready to give up; Loggins told American Songwriter he played the first demo for him in the hospital that evening. Tom Dowd produced it with Loggins's road band (Tris Imboden on drums, George Hawkins on bass, Brian Mann on keyboards, Mike Hamilton on guitar), McDonald on piano and harmony vocals, and Paulinho da Costa on percussion.
notes.context: It was the lead single from Keep the Fire, released 26 September 1979, and reached 11 on the Hot 100, 17 on the adult contemporary chart and 19 on the soul chart, Loggins's first R&B chart entry. It won him Best Male Pop Vocal Performance at the February 1981 Grammys, the night Christopher Cross swept. NBC Sports used it as the theme for its NCAA basketball tournament coverage in 1980 and 1981, which suits a song about refusing to quit.

listen_for.note: McDonald's harmony, a year after he and Loggins shared the songwriting Grammy for What a Fool Believes. He also plays the piano on the track.
Paulinho da Costa's percussion on top of Tris Imboden's drums. Da Costa and McDonald are the two outside players on what is otherwise Loggins's touring band.

notes.unverified: Songfacts says Nas sampled it on 'We Will Survive' (1999); the Nas credits don't list Loggins or McDonald, so I dropped it. Keep the Fire lists three studios (Filmways/Wally Heider in Hollywood, Santa Barbara Sound, Criteria in Miami) without saying which track was cut where.
